Theme

blanket noun

also bedding, bed covers, bedclothes

classical

Traupman 122
M-O s.v. blanket
Vicipaedia s.v. Lodix

lōdīx, lōdīcis f.

noun, third declension

For the ordinary modern blanket, Traupman (p. 122), Morgan–Owens and Vicipaedia agree on lōdīx.

Other words

  • strāgulum, strāgulī n. — bed covering, a broader term

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Traupman 122: bed covers, bedding, strāgula

Examples

  • Tē lōdīce tegam?

    Shall I cover you with the blanket?composed

  • Lōdīcem affer.

    Bring the blanket.composed

  • quī nōn sub lōdīce jacēbat, sed in culcitā saliēbat, in caput sē volvēbat, cachinnābat, cervīcālia in patrem conjiciēbat

    who was not lying under the blanket but jumping on the mattress, doing somersaults, cackling and throwing the pillows at DadLibellus II, Sintra: castellum et puteus

See also bed, duvet, bedspread, electric blanket.

SourcesMorgan–Owens: blanket · Vicipaedia: Lodix · Traupman: Conversational Latin, fourth edition · Lewis & Short: lodix · Lewis & Short: stragulum · Morgan–Owens: Adumbratio

Theodōrus et pater · Ad Larem avītum, Libellī I–VII, as they stood on 7 November 2026. Examples marked “Libellus” quote those texts word for word.
